title: The Self-Image: Your Key to a Better Life
coreMove: Lasting change starts when the self-image gives your automatic mechanism a believable target, so practice realistic pictures that make better action feel self-consistent.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rocco, a client trying to act from new evidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: External change will be wasted if the old inner portrait still directs behavior.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show that physical change helps only when the person accepts it as part of the self.

exampleSpecs.audience: Jaspreet, a designer using a building plan to explain behavior
exampleSpecs.stakes: A vague wish for change cannot guide daily action.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the house blueprint analogy to show how an inner plan sets the build.

exampleSpecs.audience: Pascal, an analyst noticing a psychological set point
exampleSpecs.stakes: A brief success may be followed by self-correction back to the old norm.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the thermostat and furnace analogy to show feedback correcting toward the target.

exampleSpecs.audience: Bonnie, a sales rep replacing slogans with a believable target
exampleSpecs.stakes: Cheerful statements will not last if the accepted identity rejects them.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast surface affirmation with a self-picture the person can accept.

exampleSpecs.audience: Madeline, a student revising a learned self-picture
exampleSpecs.stakes: A remembered scene can become a fixed identity unless it is reread with care.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show that a learned self-image can be revised by new conclusions and images.

exampleSpecs.audience: Olena, a speaker installing a clear target through mental picturing
exampleSpecs.stakes: Willpower alone is too blunt for a behavior the mind has not pictured as possible.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use vivid mental picturing as the first practical step before forced behavior.
